html:
The Dutch Republic was a federal republic of seven provinces in the northern Netherlands, from 1588 to 1795, and for much of the 1600s the richest country in Europe. It is on the map from 1600 to 1715.

It was born in the Eighty Years' War, the revolt against Spanish rule led by William the Silent. The northern provinces allied in 1579 and stopped recognising a king in 1588. Each province ran its own affairs and sent delegates to the States General; a prince of Orange usually led the army as stadtholder.

Its golden age:

  • The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, built a trading empire in Asia.
  • Amsterdam had the first modern stock market at the Amsterdam Exchange and became the centre of world trade.
  • Tulip mania in 1637 was an early speculative bubble.
  • Painters such as Rembrandt worked for a market of merchants.

Spain recognised the republic in the Peace of Westphalia in 1648. Wars with England and France followed, and in 1688 the stadtholder William III became king of England. The republic fell behind Britain in the 1700s, and in 1795 French-backed revolutionaries replaced it with the Batavian Republic.
